reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in treating Bayesian continual learning as a distributional optimization problem. The natural gradient update rule ĝ_μ = σ²·g_μ arises from the Fisher information matrix’s role in defining steepest descent directions in distribution space rather than parameter space. This implies that uncertain parameters (large σ²) receive larger updates, while certain ones (small σ²) are stabilized. The Stein gradient coreset leverages SVGD to efficiently summarize historical data into a compact set of representative samples, using kernel-based transport to align empirical points with the posterior distribution. These primitives together enable a principled form of memory retention and adaptation. Failure modes include numerical instability in high-dimensional spaces due to ill-conditioned Fisher matrices and poor kernel choices leading to suboptimal coreset quality. The unified objective L_week = logloss + logloss(coreset) + λ·KL ensures coherence between prediction, memory, and regularization.
